title: Make working in the Live Work Surface feel safe
brief: Candidates occasionally report losing in-progress work in the in-product work surface (the in-browser editor behind the dev-case apply link). The team wants working in it to feel safe. You decide what that means, which loss modes matter most, and how far to go within the timebox.
repoSeed: The kp repository itself. Start from app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx and its API routes app/api/devcase/session/route.ts + app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts, and the session storage in app/_lib/db/devcase.ts.
tasks: Investigate how in-progress work can actually be lost in the Live Work Surface and decide which loss modes matter most.
Implement the protection you judge most valuable within the timebox.
Show how you verified your change works.
Keep a short DECISIONS log: for every call you made where the brief was open — what you chose, the alternative you rejected, and what you would have asked the team.

coverProbes.where: the brief's 'feel safe' — restore-on-reload vs local draft persistence vs warn-before-leave vs tighter flush cadence
coverProbes.reveals: Do they name the loss modes, pick one deliberately, and scope it — or silently build the first thing the model suggests?
decisionSpace: Restore the last flushed server state into the editor on reload (server is source of truth)
Persist a local draft (localStorage) and reconcile with the server copy on return
Prevent the loss instead: warn before unload with unflushed changes and tighten the flush path

coverProbes.where: the existing flush()/re-buffer logic and the session event log's append-only integrity contract (server-side hash chain) — naive rewrites break event ordering or the chain
coverProbes.reveals: Do they read the existing capture pipeline before changing it, or generate over it and break the observed-process contract?
decisionSpace: Work within the existing flush/event contract and leave the capture semantics untouched
Extend the contract deliberately (e.g. a restore read path) with the integrity implications written down
Rework the flush loop and accept the re-verification burden

coverProbes.where: a resilience fix that looks right but double-appends the re-buffered event batch on retry, or restores stale files over newer local edits — passes a quick manual check
coverProbes.reveals: Do they exercise the failure paths (reload mid-session, failed flush then retry, conflicting local vs server state), or trust one happy-path check?
decisionSpace: Unit-test the failure paths against the real route/db layer
Manually drive the failure paths and document the observations
Rely on a happy-path smoke check and ship

midFlightUpdate.update: Quick update from the team: we just learned a meaningful share of candidates work on flaky connections (hotel/train wifi) — offline periods of a few minutes are common, not an edge case. Whatever you build must tolerate that.
midFlightUpdate.reveals: Do they revisit the already-chosen loss-mode priority (an offline period changes which protection matters most), or bolt a retry on without reconciling the earlier decision?
